candidates.title: Notify a restaurant when an order arrives

demandEvidence.chore: Notify the restaurant operator when a new website order is placed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A student could mock one new order and prepare a notification, but no supplied implementation reference documents Make or WhatsApp delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent restaurant operators may pay for setup help; this request establishes neither buyers nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use operator-entered sample orders and draft alerts; live order intake and WhatsApp delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed trigger could prepare repeat alerts, but a person must verify the order and send each message; no running capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The public request explicitly asks for automated restaurant order notifications, but gives no frequency, input fields or implementation corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore permits a bounded proposed alert-drafting experiment, but no implementation reference is attached and the provisional mean is 4.6, below the threshold of 6.

rejected.title: Let the ChatGPT app control your phone
rejected.reason: The excerpt is only a product announcement title; it states no concrete manual chore or request that supports a demand-first experiment.

rejected.title: Scheduled count check with a one-off trigger
rejected.reason: The attached excerpt says a one-off scheduled trigger started each run. That is a reported trigger behavior, not evidence of the count-check chore in the title; the reported one-off issue does not support a repeatable service experiment.

rejected.title: Moving an AI workflow beyond a prototype
rejected.reason: The attached excerpt is general guidance about versioning, tests and access needs as workflows grow; it does not establish a specific existing chore or a request for a service.
